### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/connector-app-github`, `@objectstack/connector-mcp`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/connector-github/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx`  _(via HERE (symbol, a top-level const object))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/apps/connector-github/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **59** of **211** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9212035719b9420c11bc19f9b3192ccf06416bdc` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `62127e0b0f6af3e2df5a7bc1ab272bb6fd60105e` — the merge of head `b6312fe6f3108fe588197fd5256ba041077789cf` into base `9212035719b9420c11bc19f9b3192ccf06416bdc`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 62127e0b0f6af3e2df5a7bc1ab272bb6fd60105e && git checkout 62127e0b0f6af3e2df5a7bc1ab272bb6fd60105e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9212035719b9420c11bc19f9b3192ccf06416bdc b6312fe6f3108fe588197fd5256ba041077789cf && git checkout -B drift-repro 9212035719b9420c11bc19f9b3192ccf06416bdc && git merge --no-ff b6312fe6f3108fe588197fd5256ba041077789cf

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9212035719b9420c11bc19f9b3192ccf06416bdc
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 9212035719b9420c11bc19f9b3192ccf06416bdc` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b6312fe6f3108fe588197fd5256ba041077789cf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts (`credentialSent`, the `include` refusal's two branches, `credentialVerified`), packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider-errors.ts (the TSDoc of `CONNECTOR_CREDENTIAL_REJECTED`, `ConnectorCredentialRejectedError` and its `status`; no type or value changes), packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-connector-credential.object.ts (the `status` description), content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx (the `include` paragraph, the refused-credential paragraph, two failure-table rows), packages/apps/connector-github/README.md (the Credentials paragraph), packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-include-credential-scope.test.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/vitest.config.ts, packages/connectors/connector-mcp/package.json (three devDependencies) + pnpm-lock.yaml, .changeset/28311-mcp-include-scope-hidden-tools.md; read on `main` for the marker's meaning and not reviewed: packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts (`isConnectorCredentialRejected` at :2450, `holdConnectorForRejectedCredential` at :3166 to :3250)

Inputs: card #28311 (body, the dev note 6538998021, triage 6539260047 which routes the credentialed case to the credential path, the claim), PR #28357 (body, the docs-drift comment, the seat's hand-off 6539986174 naming the question this record must answer, the file list of 10 files, the diff of 569 lines against `main` read whole, the seven commits from the merge-base), #27401 (the precedent the hand-off cites: a marker borrowed for a case whose retry and log semantics it did not describe, sent back to the maintainer), the 71 check-runs on this head (read 2026-10-31T06:47Z: all 71 runs completed, none failed, none cancelled, none in progress; success: Build & E2E UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint UI, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path), Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test Core, Test Core (all 8), Test UI, Test UI (all 16), Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, Validate Package Dependencies, filter; skipped: 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), Auto Label, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix shard/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in), Schedule gate · skip when a green push run covers the commit, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), UI Published Artifacts), and the tree on `main` for the marker's declared contract and the materializer's handling of it. The head is mergeable and clean against today's `main` (merge-tree clean); `main` moved `connectors.mdx` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` since the merge-base and the merge is clean.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The hand-off's question: a truthful, closed widening of the marker, not the #27401 class** - yes. The marker's declared meaning on `main` is the outcome, not the status: "neither an authoring fault nor an operational one; the upstream answered, and retrying the same value cannot change its answer", with the materializer degrading, holding a stored value as `rejected` until it is set again, the declaration changes or the process restarts, and retrying an environment or vault value on the backoff. A server that was sent the credential and lists fewer tools than `include` names is exactly that outcome: the answer was given to this credential, the same value gets the same answer, and the administrator who supplies the value is the one who can change it. The materializer's handling (`holdConnectorForRejectedCredential`, read on `main`) is the behaviour the card and triage 6539260047 prescribe for this case, so the marker is not borrowed for semantics it does not carry; in #27401 the borrowed code's backoff and "upstream unavailable" log described the case falsely, which is why it went back. The TSDoc is widened in words that name the one new raiser (an MCP server that lists only the tools a credential may use), so the contract reads true after the change; no type, value or `code` moves.
- **The predicate is the one the provider already used** - right. `credentialSent` is the former `credentialVerified` expression (`http` transport and `sendsInstanceAuth(ctx.auth)`), so the credentialed branch fires only when the instance's `auth` reached the server as a header; an `api-key` as a query parameter, a `stdio` transport, no `auth`, or a credential written into `transport.headers` (part of the declaration) keep the plain fault with a byte-identical message. The five controls pin each.
- **Status 403, and the message** - right. The server answered 2xx and refused nothing in words, and 403 is what a credential short of the scopes a resource needs is answered with (RFC 6750 section 3.1, `insufficient_scope`; GitHub's own server answers an out-of-scope `tools/call` that way). The message names the missing tools, the tools listed for this credential, and both causes with their fixes; it quotes no HTTP status and no credential (`withoutCredentialThrown` scrubs the thrown value in the materializer in any case). The dev measured that GitHub's `tools/list` answer carries no field or header about hidden tools, so "both causes" is the truthful message.
- **Downstream texts follow** - right. The `sys_connector_credential.status` description names the second way a row becomes `rejected`; the connectors page's `include` paragraph, refused-credential paragraph and two failure-table rows state the split; the GitHub README no longer says an environment-variable token stops the server, and corrects itself on which of the app's own tools GitHub hides (none: `search_issues` and `issue_read` are public-read, which the dev read at `f2a07cd1`).
- **Tests and their closure** - right. The new file runs the real provider, materializer and credential store (ObjectQL over SQLite), which is why `connector-mcp` gains three workspace devDependencies and a `vitest.config.ts` that aliases them to source (`check:test-source-alias`), disarms the console intercept and quiets the registry log through `OS_REGISTRY_LOG` (both repo gates). Nine cases: the credentialed refusal, five controls, the environment path through the materializer (degraded, listed `rejected` / `env`, recovers on a reconcile), the stored path (row `rejected`, held as `credential`, a better value recovers it), and the ablation of `if (credentialSent)` reds the three credential cases alone. The lock file carries the three links only.
- **Accept-set: nothing an author writes moves** - right. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right.
- **Check-runs as gate verdicts** - read as above; every run on this head completed and none is red, cancelled or in progress at the read.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/connector-mcp` patch, `@objectstack/service-automation` patch** - accepted. A refusal reclassified on one path, a description text; no `@objectstack/spec` entry for a TSDoc-only edit, the lane's precedent (#28346).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **A credentialed instance with a real typo in `include` now marks its stored credential `rejected`** - the message names the declaration cause, and an edit of the declaration re-attempts the instance and clears the mark on a handshake that lists every entry (`markVerified`), as the body says and the hold contract on `main` describes. A false `rejected` mark on a good credential until then is the cost of a server that cannot say which cause; named, accepted.
- **The hold log line still says "refused its credential"** - `plugin.ts` is untouched; at materialization `takeDown: false` so the dematerialize line is not reached, and the held reason is the provider's own message. Reads acceptably; a later wording card if the lane wants "refused or withheld".
- **Serial overlap** - `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx` with #28346 (PASS, different sections) and #28317 (dirty against `main`); `pnpm-lock.yaml` with anything that touches it. Whichever lands second merges `main`.
- **No name approval owed** - no new key, state or code.

### ④ Design judgment

- **Nothing blocking, no should-fix on the diff.** Tried: a server that lists every tool for an under-scoped token and refuses at `tools/call` (unchanged: the call-time 403 already takes the credential path through `credentialRefusals`); an `include` of zero missing tools (the branch is not reached); a server that hides tools from an api-key sent as a query parameter (not `credentialSent`, plain fault, the administrator's fix is the declaration or moving the key to a header, which the docs' split implies). One predicate reused, one existing marker with its existing handling, the plain fault kept for every case the credential did not reach: the smallest truthful shape.

**Verdict reasoning.** The marker's contract on `main` is defined by its outcome and handling, both of which this case satisfies, and the TSDoc now names the second raiser, so the widening is truthful and closed rather than a borrowed code; the split is keyed on the predicate the provider already trusted, the message carries both causes because the server cannot tell them apart, every path is pinned on the real stack with controls and an ablation, and every check is green or skipped on a head clean against `main`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-28311-mcp-scope-hidden-tools`
Reviewed-by: `session_01L9qibw58ehQ2gRHP2h2Puz`

**VERDICT: PASS**
